Each year countries that export a resource supply those that import it, and provinces with surplus harvests supply those that cannot feed themselves. Freight on imports depends on distance, mode, the efficiency of carriers against the world average and war; if it rises, the health of the country's retail trade and industry falls a little.

Fleet = branches × units (12 trucks, 2 ships or 1 plane per branch); each branch covers one route in the network (up to 8). With all your routes covered demand rises up to +12 %; without routes it falls 8 %. Each month each route can be delayed (~3.5 %) or lose the shipment (~0.5 %; more with low reputation or war): a delay costs 0.3 reputation; a loss, 1.5 and 3 % of the month's sales.

The treasury puts up the capital (0.03 %, 0.1 % or 0.3 % of GDP) and an annual budget (0 %, 3 % or 6 % of the capital; 70 % becomes capital and moves efficiency). Sales = capital ÷ capital intensity of the line × demand (sector health and province prosperity) × √efficiency. The result goes to the treasury. It moves the health of its sector (focused on profitability), employment and its province's GDP (value added × 0.5). After 2 years with a margin below −5 % it goes bankrupt.
